FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: dal
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} cooked until they fall apart, then woken with a tempering: {1_coll} and {2_coll} fried for a handful of seconds in scalding butter and poured over, still hissing.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: biryani
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} half-cooked and marinated {1_coll} built up in layers, sealed under a lid luted with dough, and finished smothered. It is never stirred: every layer must still be distinct when it is opened.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: butter chicken
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} put first through a scorching oven, then returned to a {1_adj} sauce mounted with {2_plur} and cream. Invented to use up the previous day's leftovers, and now the most ordered dish in the country.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: samosa
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: triangles of {0_adj} pastry filled with crushed {1_plur} and {2_plur}, sealed with water and fried gently so that the crust stays blistered rather than smooth.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: raita
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} beaten with grated {1_coll} and {2_coll} toasted dry. It is not a side dish: it is the fire extinguisher of the meal.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: palak paneer
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} blanched then ground into a green purée kept brief so as not to brown, into which are set cubes of fresh {1_adj} that do not melt.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: chana masala
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} stewed in a base of {2_adj} browned at length and {1_adj}, soured with tamarind and amchoor. The sauce should cling to the peas, not bathe them.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: vindaloo
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} marinated in {2_adj} vinegar and {1_plur}, a Portuguese inheritance of Goa. The name comes from vinha d'alhos — wine and garlic — and not from the word for potato, whatever it may look like.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: rogan josh
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} braised with {1_plur} and {2_plur} from Kashmir, which give a scarlet colour with almost no fire at all. Red and hot do not always go together.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: tandoori {0_adj}
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} scored down to the bone, marinated overnight in {1_plur} and {2_plur}, then slapped against the wall of a clay oven heated red. The yoghurt holds the marinade on and tenderises the flesh.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: pakora
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {1_coll} coated in a {0_adj} batter lifted with {2_plur} and fried in irregular clumps. Gluten-free by accident, crisp by design.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: gulab jamun
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} reduced for hours into a solid paste, rolled into balls, fried very gently, and left to drink up a {1_adj} syrup scented with rose. They have to run when you bite them.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: {0_adj} chutney
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} cooked with {1_plur}, vinegar and {2_plur} until candied. It keeps for months and improves over the first weeks.
